sentences.text:
Criminal Petition No.12106 of 2025 is filed by the petitioners- accused Nos.1 to 3 seeking to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.215 of 2025 on the file of Nallakunta Police Station,
Hyderabad, registered for the offences under Sections 329(4), 352, 351(2) and 133 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNS'); and Criminal Petition No.12108 of 2025 is filed by the petitioners- accused Nos.1, 2, 6 and 7 seeking to quash the proceedings in Crime No.231 of 2024 on the file of Nallakunta Police Station, Hyderabad, registered for the offences under Sections 420, 467,
468, 471, 474, 477-A and 506 IPC.
2.
Since the petitioners in both the petitions and the subject matter in both the petitions are one and the same, both these petitions are disposed of by this common order.

3. Heard Mr.Syed Ashfaq Ahmed, learned counsel for the petitioners in both the petitions and Ms.Shalini Saxena, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1-State.
2 ETD,J Crl.P. Nos.12106 & 12108 of 2025 4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the matter is purely of civil nature and the petitioners are facing false allegations that they have created lease deeds and collected loans from the tenant and further that they have intimidated the other tenants.
He further submitted that the petitioner No.1 in Crl.P. No.12108 of 2025 is tenant under a lease with the Trust i.e. the de facto complainant and there is no other relationship between both of them.
An eviction suit was filed by the Trust, which got compromised.
Subsequently, the present complaint is filed with a malafide intention to evict the petitioners and to strike a deal.
He further submitted that the petitioners have filed O.S. No.4264 of 2025 and have obtained status quo order pursuant to which these complaints are filed as a counter blast.

Ever since then, the police are harassing the petitioners and under the guise of these complaints, the de facto complainant is forcing petitioner No.1 and his sons to sign on the agreement according to their own terms and hence, he prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor has submitted that petitioners in Crl.P. No.12108 of 2025 have tress-passed into the land and created lease deed and the petitioners in Crl.P. No.12106 of 2025 have trespassed into the land and caused obstruction to the 3 ETD,J Crl.P. Nos.12106 & 12108 of 2025 construction of a new building, which is being constructed as per the sanctioned plan and created nuisance by entering into the premises with criminal force and threatened them with dire consequences.

He further has submitted that since the prima facie case is made out against the Mr. Mamidala Rajulu vs The State Of Telangana on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162002558/
1 petitioners, the proceedings against them cannot be quashed and hence, prayed to dismiss the petitions.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Perused the record.
7.
Admittedly, the petitioners are the lessees under the de facto complainant Trust.
Pendency of the suit i.e. O.S No.4264 of 2023 shows that there is civil dispute between both the parties.

Though the learned counsel for the petitioners claims that there is an order granted by the trial court in favour of the petitioners, it is a status quo order which imposes a responsibility on both the parties equally to maintain status quo with regard to the suit schedule property.

However, the allegations point out prima facie case against the petitioners in Crl.P. No.12106 of 2025 for the offences under Sections 329(4), 352, 351(2) and 133 of BNS and for the offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 474,
477-A and 506 IPC against the petitioners in Crl.P. No.10108 of 2025.
The investigation is still in progress.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said process.

Though the learned counsel for the 4 ETD,J Crl.P. Nos.12106 & 12108 of 2025 petitioners contends that the matter is civil in nature and can be pursued by civil remedies in a civil court, the creation of documents involves criminality and thus, it cannot be held as a ground to quash the proceedings as per the decision in Kathayayini v. Sidharth P.S. Reddy and others 1.
8.

entities.text: Kathayayini v. Sidharth P.S. Reddy and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in the light of the above said decision and in view of the above held discussion, the criminal petitions lack merit and hence, both the petitions are dismissed.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
